key_insight: SHAP-selected turbulent regions outside classical structure masks are less energetic but show more unexpected velocity transitions, revealing predictive information beyond instantaneous coherent structures.
engineering_relevance: Combining SHAP with conditional surprisal could help assess whether turbulence-prediction models capture informative flow dynamics beyond energetic structures.
method: Study turbulent channel flow at friction Reynolds numbers Reτ ≈ 125 and 550.
Compare SHAP-selected regions with classical structure masks using state-conditioned velocity-transition surprisal.
Analyze internal u = 0 interfaces and compare surfaces after matching fluctuation energy.
evidence_signal: Near the wall, at comparable fluctuation energy and wall distance, high-surprisal voxels outside classical masks were approximately 11× and 5× more likely to be SHAP-selected at Reτ ≈ 125 and 550, respectively.
watch_item: Raw interfacial surprisal excess is largely associated with surrounding fluctuation energy; after energy matching, the equally weighted surface comparison is statistically compatible with unity on retained common support.
paper_title: What explainable deep learning reveals about wall-bounded turbulence: insights from conditional surprisal
